article.title: When a Good KPI Creates Bad Behavior

paragraphs.en: A metric can improve while the underlying business becomes worse. If a support team is rewarded only for reducing handling time, staff may close difficult cases too quickly. If a sales team is measured only by the number of new accounts, it may acquire customers who never become active. The problem is not measurement itself but the gap between the proxy and the intended outcome. Balanced metrics and regular review can reduce these distortions.
paragraphs.zh: 本段討論「When a Good KPI Creates Bad Behavior」的實務含義：先理解問題與決策背景。 重要的是將觀察到的現象與真正需要採取的行動分開，並留下可供驗證的依據。
paragraphs.ja: 「When a Good KPI Creates Bad Behavior」について、業務上の前提と意思決定を確認する。まず課題と背景を理解する。 観察事実と実際に取るべき行動を区別し、検証可能な根拠を残すことが重要である。

paragraphs.en: One defense is to pair a speed metric with a quality measure. Customer service teams can track resolution time alongside repeat contacts and satisfaction. Sales teams can track account creation alongside activation and retention. The metrics should be reviewed together because optimizing one number in isolation can shift costs elsewhere. Qualitative investigation remains important when the numbers disagree.
